title: Empirical Evaluation of a Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Pipeline: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt‑5‑mini on 400 Intent→Configuration Tasks
abstract: We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002) and executed a paired experiment measuring operational failures when applying LLM‑generated configuration changes directly (Baseline) versus applying a deterministic syntax/policy validator with at most one bounded LLM repair (Guarded). Using gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted NetOps adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) on 400 public/synthetic intents (shared_initial_candidate generation semantics, one shared candidate per paired episode), the run completed 800 episodes with no infrastructure failures. All 400 paired episodes were operationally successful under both arms (n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The paired difference (Guarded − Baseline)=0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI 0.00–0.00; 10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p=1.0. Important interpretation: because generation_semantics was preregistered as shared_initial_candidate and the deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0, deterministic_repair_calls_invoked=0), the Guarded intervention was empirically inert on this task bank. We release full archived artifacts and hashes (execution_manifest) and interpret these results as a reproducible boundary case that highlights how generation semantics and task sampling determine whether a validator can be meaningfully exercised.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→CLI translation with generative LLMs promises NetOps productivity gains but introduces operational risk: erroneous device commands can cause reachability loss, policy violations, and outages. Prior work therefore recommends generate→validate→repair architectures with bounded repair budgets or human approval. Yet there is little preregistered, artifact‑grounded evidence quantifying real failure rates and the protective value of lightweight automated validators. We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002) a paired experiment to measure whether a deterministic syntax/policy validator (with ≤1 deterministic LLM repair) reduces operational failure proportion compared to direct application of an LLM candidate. Our run is fully archived: prompts, model calls, validator logs, emulator scores, and SHA‑256 manifests are published in the execution manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865). The principal contribution is a reproducible, preregistered execution and a frank, artifact‑grounded account of a boundary outcome where the Guarded intervention was inert.
sections.related_work: We position this experiment amid recent work on LLMs for NetOps/AIOps and verifier‑guided repair. Representative verified sources that informed design include: a comprehensive survey on LLM‑based network management and evaluation (W4415071524), intent→configuration translation using LLMs (doi:10.1002/nem.2313), verifier‑guided IaC repair studies (doi:10.2139/ssrn.6608518; W7124141852), and proposals for bounded execution and formal verification primitives in NetOps (W4401857375). These works motivate bounded repair budgets and workflow‑centred evaluation. Our study differs by preregistering an explicit paired estimand and by releasing the full execution archive enabling exact reproducibility.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. Before any model calls we froze CAND‑2026‑002: research question, confirmatory hypotheses H1–H4, primary estimand (paired difference in operational failure proportion), sample size (400 paired intents), analysis plan (McNemar exact test; 10,000 bootstrap percentile CI, seed=1729), maximum model calls (800), generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation=false), and retry policy. The preregistration is archived in execution_manifest. Pipeline. For each intent we issued one shared generation call to gpt‑5‑mini (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) producing a single configuration candidate used by both conditions (shared_initial_candidate). Baseline: apply candidate directly. Guarded: run deterministic syntax/policy validator against the same shared candidate; on validator rejection (none observed) permit at most one deterministic LLM repair call per preregistration. Emulation and scoring. Sandboxed emulator replicas applied the candidate changes and an automated scorer flagged operational failure (reachability loss or policy violation). All raw outputs, per‑task scoring JSONs, provider call logs, and validator traces are archived (see execution_manifest paths and hashes). Analysis plan. Primary test: paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00), McNemar exact two‑sided test, and 95% bootstrap percentile CI for the paired difference (10k resamples, seed=1729). Secondary analyses (outage duration, rollback counts, vendor/change‑type subgroups) were preregistered but conditional on observed failures.
sections.results: Execution statistics and principal numbers (artifact pointers): completed episodes=800; completed_pair_count=400; model_calls_used=400; validator_reject_count=0; deterministic_repair_calls_invoked=0. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf) shows n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Observed rates: baseline_success=400/400=1.0; guarded_success=400/400=1.0. Confirmatory statistics: paired difference (Guarded − Baseline)=0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.00,0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p=1.0. Per‑intent traces, model outputs and scoring JSONs are archived under execution/responses/ and execution/scoring/ (see execution_manifest for full file lists and SHA‑256s). Crucial diagnostic: because generation_semantics was preregistered as shared_initial_candidate, both arms received identical candidates and the deterministic validator accepted every candidate (validator_reject_count=0); thus no repair or validator effect could arise on this task bank.
sections.discussion: Boundary‑case interpretation. The run's arithmetic and archived artifacts are correct and reproducible. However the outcome is a boundary case: the preregistered choice of shared_initial_candidate plus a validator that did not reject any preserved candidate made the Guarded intervention empirically inert. Consequently the confirmatory test did not exercise validator efficacy on this task set. This is an informative methodological result: to evaluate a validator’s protective value one must design for a nonzero expected validator firing rate (e.g., use independent per‑condition generation, include a small fraction of injected positive controls, or select a task bank calibrated for validator rejects). Reviewer requests addressed. Per reviewer instruction we (1) expose validator rules and decision logs (execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/transformation_manifest.json) so readers can inspect why rejects did not occur, (2) provide exact artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes for principal numbers (raw results: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865; paired contingency: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf), and (3) include representative prompt→shared candidate→validator pass→scorer JSON traces (execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt and execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json; see execution_manifest). Sensitivity and limitations. Archived scoring JSONs contain no near‑failure examples; therefore we cannot use the preserved artifacts alone to demonstrate scorer false negatives or validator blind spots. This inability is an explicit limitation; post‑hoc injection or reruns would be required to test validator sensitivity. Design guidance. Future preregistered evaluations seeking to measure validator impact should: (i) use independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation=true) so each arm may produce distinct candidates, (ii) include injected positive controls to verify validator liveness, or (iii) sample tasks known to produce nontrivial validator rejects. External validity. This study used a single model (gpt‑5‑mini), a single adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1), public/synthetic intents and emulator replicas; findings do not generalize beyond these precise conditions.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully archived, preregistered paired evaluation (CAND‑2026‑002) that compared direct application of LLM‑generated configurations with a deterministic validator+≤1 repair pipeline on 400 intent→configuration tasks. The reproducible boundary outcome (n11=400; validator_reject_count=0; repair_calls=0) shows that generation semantics and task selection can render a guarded validator empirically inert. The scientific contribution is methodological: we document a transparent boundary case and provide concrete design lessons for future preregistered NetOps evaluations. All artifacts, exact file paths, and SHA‑256 hashes are released to enable exact reproduction and to support follow‑on preregistered runs that vary generation semantics, task sampling, or validator configuration.

disclosure_statement: Mandatory disclosure (artifact‑grounded). Human role and autonomy boundary: after an autonomy lock the autonomous system conducted the literature review, experimental design, preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002), execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI‑peer review response, and revision. The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved autonomy boundaries and pre‑lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. LLM(s) and adapter: model=gpt‑5‑mini (used via a hosted NetOps adapter identified as hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Exact initial master prompt(s), system instructions, and generation templates are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865) and in execution/transformation_manifest.json (hash recorded in the execution_manifest). Preregistration/freeze: the preregistration CAND‑2026‑002 (frozen before model calls) specified the research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1–H4), primary and secondary estimands, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), per‑intent paired design, analysis plan (McNemar exact test and bootstrap CIs), seeds (bootstrap seed=1729), retry policy, and maximum model calls (800). These elements are archived (preregistration object in execution_manifest). Framework and tools: experiments used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family to call gpt‑5‑mini; deterministic validator implementation, repair template, and emulator scoring harness are archived (execution/execution_log.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json). What was archived: every prompt, provider call, model output, validator decision, tool call, raw execution log, per‑task scoring JSON, and SHA‑256 manifest (see execution_manifest for each file and hash). Technical restarts and failures: the execution_manifest records started_at_utc and completed_at_utc; completed_episode_count=800, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=400. Pre‑lock development: prior infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence; no pre‑lock experimental outcomes were used as final evidence. Post‑run artifacts: analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg) and the analysis log are archived; principal artifact hashes include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf. Important interpretive note required by the run: the preregistered generation_semantics was shared_initial_candidate (one identical candidate generated per paired episode) and the deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0). Consequently the Guarded pipeline was inert in this execution (no repair calls invoked), producing perfect concordance (n11=400). This outcome is fully traceable in the archived artifacts and is reported above as a documented boundary case. All archived artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes are released to enable reproducibility and to permit follow‑on preregistered experiments that vary generation semantics, task sampling, or validator configuration.
limitations: Single‑model and single‑adapter: only gpt‑5‑mini with hosted_netops_gvr_v1 was used; results do not generalize to other LLMs/adapters.

Generation semantics choice (shared_initial_candidate) made the Guarded intervention empirically inert in this execution (validator_reject_count=0), preventing the preregistered hypotheses from being tested on these tasks.
Task bank and emulation: public/synthetic intents in sandboxed emulator replicas do not fully represent production heterogeneity or adversarial inputs.

No preserved injected positive controls: archived scoring JSONs show no observed near‑failures, so post‑hoc assessment of scorer/validator false negatives is not possible from the preserved artifacts alone.
Vendor/device fidelity: emulator replicas and vendor models are approximations; broader vendor and hardware validation is required before operational claims.
